scope.q: What is the acceptable false negative rate for identifying liability clauses, given the critical nature of these clauses?
scope.why: Understanding the tolerance for missing critical clauses is paramount to designing the system's accuracy and review workflow.

scope.q: Beyond 'liability clauses,' what specific sub-types or patterns within these clauses need to be identified and extracted (e.g., indemnification, limitation of liability, warranty disclaimers)?
scope.why: Defining the precise scope of 'liability clauses' is crucial for training data creation and model specificity.

scope.q: What is the desired end-state for the legal team's workflow after using this tool, e.g., does it flag clauses for review, auto-summarize, or suggest redlines?
scope.why: Knowing the desired integration and output format will dictate the system's interface and functionality.

decomposition.title: Document Ingestion & Preprocessing
decomposition.why: Contracts come in various formats, so a robust system to handle diverse inputs and prepare them for analysis is necessary.

decomposition.title: Clause Identification & Extraction
decomposition.why: This core component is responsible for accurately finding and isolating all relevant liability-related clauses within the contract text.

decomposition.title: Clause Analysis & Risk Scoring
decomposition.why: Beyond just extraction, the system needs to interpret the content of identified clauses and assign a risk level or highlight specific terms.

decomposition.title: Human-in-the-Loop Review Interface
decomposition.why: Given the 'cannot be wrong' constraint, a user-friendly interface for legal professionals to review, correct, and provide feedback is essential.

decomposition.title: Feedback & Model Retraining Pipeline
decomposition.why: Continuous improvement requires a structured way to capture human corrections and use them to refine the underlying AI models.

sprint.title: Set up Ingestion & Text Extraction
sprint.deliv: POC ingests 5 diverse contracts (PDF, DOCX, image) and extracts clean text into a temporary store.

sprint.title: Initial Clause Identification Model
sprint.deliv: A basic NLP model (e.g., keyword-based + simple ML) identifies 3 common liability clause types in 10 test contracts.

sprint.title: Basic Review UI & Feedback Loop
sprint.deliv: Web interface displays extracted clauses for 5 contracts, allowing legal users to mark as correct/incorrect and add comments.

sprint.title: Enhanced Clause Analysis
sprint.deliv: Model distinguishes between 'indemnification' and 'limitation of liability' with 80% accuracy on a held-out set.

sprint.title: End-to-End Workflow Demo
sprint.deliv: Demonstrate ingesting a new contract, automatic clause flagging, and a legal user reviewing and submitting feedback.

sprint.title: Model Retraining Pipeline Setup
sprint.deliv: Automated script retrains the clause identification model using collected feedback data, showing improved performance on new data.

risks.risk: False negatives on critical liability clauses could lead to significant legal exposure for the customer.
risks.mitigation: Implement a 'human-in-the-loop' workflow where all identified liability clauses (and potentially surrounding text) are presented to the legal team for mandatory review and sign-off, prioritizing recall over precision initially.

risks.risk: The variability in contract language and structure across different vendors will degrade model performance.
risks.mitigation: Start with a diverse, representative dataset of historical contracts for initial training. Continuously collect and integrate feedback from legal team reviews to fine-tune the model on edge cases and new contract types.

risks.risk: OCR accuracy for scanned or poor-quality documents may lead to incomplete or incorrect text extraction, impacting downstream analysis.
risks.mitigation: Integrate a robust, commercially available OCR solution with confidence scoring. Implement a 'flag for manual review' mechanism for documents with low OCR confidence or significant extraction errors.

risks.risk: Defining 'liability clauses' too broadly will result in excessive false positives, overwhelming the legal team.
risks.mitigation: Work closely with the legal team to iteratively refine the definition and specific sub-types of liability clauses to be identified. Implement a configurable confidence threshold for flagging clauses, allowing the legal team to adjust the balance between recall and precision.
